answer: Invitations form a quota tree. Each identity vouches for at most two recruits per epoch, and its own quota drops 0.2 for every recruit that fails a panel. Failed answers re-queue to a second panel instead of being dropped, so the same evidence is graded twice. The number that matters is the delta, since a cedar-top account with three bad recruits loses more quota than a fresh one ever had. Cascading that damage down a canyon of branches, then seeding a plume of new identities, costs more keys than a farm can fund.
